newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RESEARCH ALERT-Portman Mining seen a 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Portman Mining seen a 'buy'.

text.p: Wilson HTM Ltd was recommending emerging coal producer Portman Mining Ltd as a buy reflecting the group's attractive long-term fundamentals.
"Buy for production expansion benefits. (The group) is trading on an attractive 1999 price-earnings valuation," Wilson analyst Corey Nolan said in an overview report on the Australian coal sector.
The Australian coal industry had historically focused on volume growth with less importance placed on rates of return and profitability, Nolan said.
"More recently we have seen the emergence of the small producer.
"Portman and CIM Resources revolutionised the industry with their profit focus and success," Nolan said.
Portman and CIM currently had the highest forecast operating margins in the sector, Nolan said.
He recommended CIM as an accumulate investment, while rating Australia Coal Ltd as a speculative buy.
Nolan said the medium to longer-term outlook for coal prices was seen as relatively flat and mainly affected by supply and demand factors.
Wilson HTM rated coal majors, QCT Resources Ltd and Coal and Allied Industries Ltd as "holds."
"Coal and Allied is going through a difficult time with industrial problems and is rated a 'hold' given the potential for this operation to be turned around," Nolan said.
QCT had good margins and was well traded due to its size and liquidity, Nolan said.

Prices at the time of the report showed Portman at A$3.20, compared with A$2.90 at Friday, CIM at 59 cents, the same as Friday's close and Austral Coal at 53 cents, compared with 50 cents at Friday's close.
Coal and Allied shares were at $9.40, compared with Friday's close at A$9.20, while QCT was at $1.62, compared with A$1.60 at today's close.
